Get started with kelpbio

Source: vignettes/kelpbio.Rmd
kelpbio.Rmd
library(kelpbio)
library(ggplot2)

kelpbio estimates the biomass of Nereocystis luetkeana and Macrocystis pyrifera. Total biomass combines plants counted and measured in in situ surveys, the surface canopy area mapped from aerial imagery, and a calibration model that relates the two. See the Methods article for more details on methods, including expected survey design and timing, general statistical approach, model descriptions, and how sub-models are combined to get predictions.

This article uses Nereocystis as an example. The data shown below are simulated, with invented site names.

Glossary

  • Plant: one individual (sporophyte), identified by its holdfast (Macrocystis) or stipe (Nereocystis).
  • In situ survey: count of the plants within a surveyed area, with all or a sample of the plants measured (e.g., three 30 m sub-surface transects with 2 m swaths, and the maximum sub-bulb diameter measured for 15 plants per transect).
  • Plot: area bounding the in situ survey, over which canopy percent cover is calculated.
  • Canopy map: surface canopy within a site mapped from aerial imagery, with the tide height recorded at the time of imaging.
  • Site: a location of any size with mapped canopy and possibly, matching in situ survey data.
  • Site-year: annual snapshot of a site, i.e., in peak season.

Data format

Each dataset is a table with a set of required column names and values, formatted for model fitting. Expected units are in the column names (e.g., diameter_mm). The Data format article describes what each dataset holds, how the datasets are linked, and their columns, as given by kb_data_columns(). Each dataset has a kb_check_data_*() function that checks it.

Fit a model

The weight model relates plant weight to diameter, allowing for differences among sites and years.

fit <- kb_fit_weight_nereo(data_weight_sim_nereo)

kb_model_describe() prints a detailed description of the fitted model, including its priors. kb_stancode() prints the underlying Stan code.

kb_model_describe(fit)
#> Weight allometry - Nereocystis luetkeana
#> Response: wet weight (kg); predictor: plant diameter (mm)
#> 
#> Likelihood
#>   log(weight_kg) ~ Normal(log(mu), sd_residual)
#>   mu = weight_floor + alpha * x^diameter_power
#>   log(alpha) = intercept
#>              + site_effect[site]
#>              + year_effect[year]
#>              + site_year_effect[site, year]
#>   x = diameter_mm / d0,  d0 = 24.9  (geometric mean diameter)
#> 
#> Random effects
#>   site_effect[site]            ~ Normal(0, sd_site)       site effect on log(alpha)
#>   year_effect[year]            ~ Normal(0, sd_year)       year effect on log(alpha)
#>   site_year_effect[site, year] ~ Normal(0, sd_site_year)  site:year effect on log(alpha)
#> 
#> Priors
#>   intercept      ~ Normal(0, 2)
#>   diameter_power ~ Normal(2, 1) T[0, ]
#>   weight_floor   ~ Normal(0, 0.5) T[0, ]
#>   sd_residual    ~ Exponential(1)
#>   sd_site        ~ Exponential(1)
#>   sd_year        ~ Exponential(1)
#>   sd_site_year   ~ Exponential(1)

tidy() or coef() gives the estimate of each parameter with its lower and upper 95% compatibility limits.

tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 4
#>   term           estimate    lower  upper
#>   <chr>             <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 intercept       -0.666  -0.918   -0.421
#> 2 diameter_power   2.92    2.71     3.13 
#> 3 weight_floor     0.118   0.098    0.14 
#> 4 sd_site          0.2     0.0406   0.521
#> 5 sd_year          0.0544  0.00298  0.254
#> 6 sd_site_year     0.261   0.179    0.372
#> 7 sd_residual      0.463   0.438    0.488

Model convergence can be checked with glance() or kb_converged(). A converged model must meet thresholds for R-hat, effective sample size (ESS), and divergent transitions. See ?kb_converged for definitions and suggestions for resolving convergence failures.

glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>       n     K nchains niters nthin ess_bulk ess_tail  rhat perc_divergent
#>   <int> <int>   <int>  <dbl> <int>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1   660     7       3    500     4     733.     589.  1.00              0
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: converged <lgl>

In a converged model, the chains of each parameter overlap and should resemble a ‘fuzzy caterpillar’.

kb_plot_trace(fit)

See the advanced usage article for more diagnostics.

Predict and plot

The kb_predict_*() functions take a fit object and generate predictions (estimates with 95% compatibility limits).

If no new data are supplied, predictions are made for each row of the data the model was fitted to.

kb_predict_weight(fit)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 660 × 8
#>    diameter_mm weight_kg site       year  weight_support estimate lower upper
#>          <dbl>     <dbl> <fct>      <fct> <chr>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1        28.6     0.663 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.779 0.632 0.96 
#>  2        16.5     0.569 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.262 0.23  0.299
#>  3        27.3     0.841 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.697 0.567 0.855
#>  4        38.3     1.38  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.64  1.31  2.08 
#>  5        16.2     0.153 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.255 0.224 0.291
#>  6        29.8     0.793 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.861 0.697 1.06 
#>  7        34.7     1.36  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.27  1.01  1.58 
#>  8        16.2     0.141 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.255 0.224 0.291
#>  9        25.9     0.311 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.615 0.505 0.752
#> 10        35.5     1.53  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.34  1.07  1.68 
#> # ℹ 650 more rows

New data can be supplied to predict at specific values, including values not in the observed data.

new_dat <- data.frame(site = "otter_cove", year = 2023, diameter_mm = c(15, 20))
kb_predict_weight(fit, new_data = new_dat)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   site        year diameter_mm weight_support estimate lower upper
#>   <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 otter_cove  2023          15 site-year         0.242 0.213 0.277
#> 2 otter_cove  2023          20 site-year         0.388 0.321 0.469

kb_new_data() is a helper that generates a grid of new data, e.g., the full range of diameters at each site, and the predictions can be plotted with kb_plot_predictions().

predictions <- kb_predict_weight(fit, kb_new_data(fit, by = "site"))
kb_plot_predictions(predictions)

The plot is a ggplot object, so the data can be added as a layer.

kb_plot_predictions(predictions, log_axis = "xy") +
  geom_point(
    data = data_weight_sim_nereo,
    aes(x = diameter_mm, y = weight_kg),
    alpha = 0.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  )

See the advanced usage article for control over how uncertainty is estimated for a new site or year (i.e., one not in the data the model was fitted to).

From plants to total biomass

In situ biomass

The biomass (kg/m²) of an in situ survey is the number of plants counted times their mean weight, over the area surveyed. Mean weight is estimated, with uncertainty, from the weight model and a size model fitted to a sample of measured plants (see Censused areas for surveys where all plants are measured).

fit_size <- kb_fit_size_nereo(data_size_sample_sim_nereo)
data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo
#> # A tibble: 54 × 8
#>    survey_id       site  year  survey_area_m2 plants plot_area_m2 canopy_area_m2
#>    <chr>           <fct> <fct>          <dbl>  <int>        <dbl>          <dbl>
#>  1 otter_cove-202… otte… 2020            140     992         215            87.3

#>  3 gull_rock-2020… gull… 2020            233.    660         233.           30.3
#>  4 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020             40       0         270.           34.3
#>  5 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020            180     861         255.           81.2
#>  6 heron_reef-202… hero… 2020            120     550         217.           73.5
#>  7 urchin_shoal-2… urch… 2020            160    1815         218.          116. 
#>  8 sculpin_head-2… scul… 2020            193.   1245         193.           30.1

set.seed(1)
biomass <- kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo,

Cover calibration

The cover calibration model relates the estimated biomass of each in situ survey to the percent cover of canopy mapped (e.g., by drone or satellite imagery) within the plot bounding the survey.

fit_cover <- kb_fit_cover_calibration_nereo(biomass)
fit_cover <- fit_cover_calibration_sim_nereo

kb_predict_cover_calibration(fit_cover, kb_new_data(fit_cover)) |>
  kb_plot_predictions()

Total biomass

The cover calibration model is applied to each canopy map to estimate its total biomass.

data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo

#>    site      year  canopy_area_m2 canopy_tide_height_m classified_area_m2 region
#>    <fct>     <fct>          <dbl>                <dbl>              <dbl> <fct> 
#>  1 otter_co… 2020            6817                 1.2               18504 north 
#>  2 gull_rock 2020           53242                 0.15             142539 north 
#>  3 cedar_bay 2020            5893                 1.05              11737 north 
#>  4 heron_re… 2020           24787                 0.6               51227 north 
#>  5 urchin_s… 2020           20431                 0.75              55633 south 
#>  6 sculpin_… 2020           16455                 1                 45632 south

#>  9 otter_co… 2021            4819                 1.6                9556 north 
#> 10 gull_rock 2021           38877                 0.2               83128 north 
#> # ℹ 39 more rows

totals <- kb_predict_biomass_canopy(fit_cover, data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo)
totals

#> # A tibble: 49 × 11

#>    <fct>     <fct>          <dbl>                <dbl>              <dbl> <fct> 
#>  1 otter_co… 2020            6817                 1.2               18504 north 
#>  2 gull_rock 2020           53242                 0.15             142539 north

#>  4 heron_re… 2020           24787                 0.6               51227 north 
#>  5 urchin_s… 2020           20431                 0.75              55633 south 
#>  6 sculpin_… 2020           16455                 1                 45632 south 
#>  7 eagle_sp… 2020           38273                 1.3               76960 south 
#>  8 tidepool… 2020           20110                 0.2               41234 south 
#>  9 otter_co… 2021            4819                 1.6                9556 north

#> #   estimate <dbl>, lower <dbl>, upper <dbl>

kb_plot_predictions(totals, geom = "bar")

pool_by pools the estimates by group, in this case to give the total biomass in each year and region, summed across sites, with the uncertainty of the sum.

set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit_cover,
  data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo,
  pool_by = c("region", "year")
) |>
  kb_plot_predictions(geom = "bar")

See the methods article for more detail, including a diagram of a typical survey layout that shows how a plot relates to its site.

Dry, carbon, and nitrogen biomass

A wet/dry model fit converts wet to dry biomass, a carbon model fit converts dry biomass to carbon, and a nitrogen model fit converts dry biomass to nitrogen.

kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit_cover,
  data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo,
  wetdry = fit_wetdry_sim_nereo,
  carbon = fit_carbon_sim_nereo,
  measure = "carbon"
)

#> # A tibble: 49 × 11

Pre-fit models

The kelpbiodata package holds public datasets, with models pre-fit to them. The pre-fit models can be used when data have not been collected at your sites for a particular sub-model, such as harvested plants for weight allometry or tissue samples for the dry:wet ratio and carbon fraction. There is a pre-fit model for every sub-model, including the cover calibration, so canopy biomass can be estimated from a canopy map alone.

set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  kelpbiodata::fit_weight_hakai_nereo,
  kelpbiodata::fit_size_hakai_nereo,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo[1:3, ],
  progress = "none"
)

Sites or years in the user’s data that are not in the pre-fit model’s dataset are treated as new levels, so their estimates have wider uncertainty.

User data can also be combined with a kelpbiodata dataset to increase the number of observations. For example, if plants have been harvested at only a couple of sites, combining them with the kelpbiodata Hakai Institute weight data gives a better estimate of the general weight allometry relationship, while the site-level random effect still gives an estimate for each site of interest from the user’s data.

data_weight <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  kelpbiodata::data_weight_hakai_nereo,
  dplyr::filter(data_weight_sim_nereo, site %in% c("otter_cove", "gull_rock"))
)

# 3 chains of 500 draws match the 1500 draws of fit_size_sim_nereo.
fit_combined <- kb_fit_weight_nereo(
  data_weight,
  chains = 3L,
  niters = 500L,
  nthin = 4L,
  seed = 1L,
  progress = "none",
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99)
)

set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_combined,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo[1:3, ],
  progress = "none"
)

Censused areas

If every plant within a survey area is counted and measured (a full census), a size model is not needed, and per_area = FALSE gives the total biomass in the surveyed area. The uncertainty in biomass then comes only from the weight model. When every plant in a site is counted and measured, no calibration is needed.

data_size_census_sim_nereo
#> # A tibble: 6,022 × 3
#>    survey_id         diameter_mm partial
#>    <chr>                   <dbl> <lgl>  
#>  1 otter_cove-2020-1        28.9 FALSE  
#>  2 otter_cove-2020-1        15.5 TRUE   
#>  3 otter_cove-2020-1        18.6 FALSE  
#>  4 otter_cove-2020-1        21.6 FALSE  
#>  5 otter_cove-2020-1        40.4 FALSE  
#>  6 otter_cove-2020-1        24.5 FALSE  
#>  7 otter_cove-2020-1        30.7 FALSE  
#>  8 otter_cove-2020-1         9.2 TRUE   
#>  9 otter_cove-2020-1        35.1 FALSE  
#> 10 otter_cove-2020-1        23.4 FALSE  
#> # ℹ 6,012 more rows

# The censused surveys, with their counts taken from the census.
census_surveys <- dplyr::filter(
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo,
  survey_id %in% data_size_census_sim_nereo$survey_id
)
census_surveys <- dplyr::select(census_surveys, -plants)

kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  data_size_census_sim_nereo,
  census_surveys,
  per_area = FALSE,
  progress = "none"
)
#> Warning: 5 values of diameter_mm lie far outside the fitted range (3.8 to 71.2).
#> ℹ Check that the values are in millimetres.

#> 5 otter_cove-2023-1 otter_cove 2023            160          269.           41.6

Macrocystis

Every counted Macrocystis plant has its fronds recorded, so a size census is always used in place of a size model. The calibration and totals follow as for Nereocystis.

set.seed(1)
biomass_macro <- kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_macro,
  data_size_census_sim_macro,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_macro,
  progress = "none"
)
